newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ENGLAND TOIL BEFORE RAIN WASHES OUT PLAY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND TOIL BEFORE RAIN WASHES OUT PLAY.

text.p: England's blushes were saved by the weather for the second successive day in the second test on Friday.
A thunderstorm which only allowed four deliveries after tea left Zimbabwe strongly placed at 93 for two in reply to England's 156.

England have been given a lesson in how to play test cricket in this match. Test minnows Zimbabwe bowled with discipline on the first day to reduce England to 137 for nine and their batsmen responded in kind, grinding out the runs from 48.4 overs.

Opener Grant Flower has so far faced 144 balls for his 33 not out and looks in the kind of mood to repeat the double century he made here against Pakistan last year, an innings which set up Zimbabwe's only test win.
England off-spinner Robert Croft was convinced he had the left-handed opener caught down the leg side when he had made 29, but the appeal was rejected and television replays proved inconclusive.
England, resuming on 137 for nine, lasted another 10 overs in the morning before Phil Tufnell was unlucky to deflect a short ball from Heath Streak on to his stumps when he had made nine.
John Crawley, alone in showing the kind of application which brought him a century in the first test in Bulawayo, was left high and dry on 47 not out from 172 balls.
Streak finished with four for 43 and medium-pacer Guy Whittall took a career-best four for 18.
Mark Dekker, drafted into the home side in place of Stuart Carlisle, was an early victim in the Zimbabwe reply, edging an Allan Mullally out-swinger to the wicketkeeper when he had made just two.
England's only other success came in the second session when Zimbabwe captain Alistair Campbell drove loosely at Craig White and was caught at first slip for 22.
Player-coach Dave Houghton survived a good lbw shout from Tufnell early in his innings but then, taking his lead from Flower, grafted his way to 26 not out before the rain.
